title: Republic of New Granada
capsule: The Republic of New Granada was constituted in 1831 after Gran Colombia dissolved, inheriting the territories of present-day Colombia, Panama, and Ecuador (until Ecuador's separation in 1830 and Venezuela's in the same year). The republic was dominated by the tension between Liberal and Conservative factions over centralism, church-state relations, and the role of the military, producing a series of civil conflicts. It was reorganized under the Liberal-backed Constitution of 1853, which abolished slavery outright and extended universal male suffrage, and formally replaced by the Granadine Confederation in 1858.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The republic's borders with Venezuela and Ecuador were in principle inherited from Gran Colombia's internal divisions, but frontier demarcation was incomplete and boundary disputes persisted throughout the period.
